description: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has classified Indian soils into 8 major categories. Soil formation is primarily influenced by the weathering of parent rocks, climate, topography, and time.

sections.title: Classification and Characteristics of Indian Soils
sections.description: General classification of soil types in India and the fundamental processes behind their formation.

key_concepts.explanation: The scientific process of soil formation, which is heavily dependent on climate, parent rock material, and biological activities over time.

Khadar refers to the new, highly fertile alluvial soil replenished annually by floods. Bhangar is the older alluvial soil found higher up the plains, often containing calcareous nodules known as 'Kankar'.

important_facts.fact: According to ICAR, Alluvial Soil is the most widespread soil type in India, covering approximately 43% of the total geographical area.
Almost all Indian soils are generally deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic matter (humus).

sections.title: Alluvial and Black Soils
sections.description: The most agriculturally significant soils, responsible for the highest crop yields in India.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Dominant in the Northern Plains and River Valleys.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Formed by the deposition of silt brought down by the Indus-Ganga-Brahmaputra river systems. It is rich in potash but generally poor in phosphorus.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Covers most of the Deccan Plateau, specifically Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Formed from the weathering of volcanic basalt rocks. It is highly rich in lime, iron, magnesium, and alumina.

key_associations.extra_info: It is exceptionally suited for cotton cultivation, hence widely known as 'Black Cotton Soil'.

important_facts.fact: Black soil possesses a very high moisture retention capacity and develops deep cracks during the dry season, aiding in aeration, a phenomenon known as 'self-ploughing'.

sections.title: Red and Laterite Soils
sections.description: Soils predominantly found in the Peninsular region, formed under varying rainfall conditions.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Eastern and Southern parts of the Deccan Plateau, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Develops on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall. It is generally porous, friable, and less fertile without fertilizers.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Western Ghats, North-East India, and Meghalaya plateaus.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall. It is very poor in humus, nitrogen, and calcium.

scientific_principles.application: The presence of ferric oxide gives Red Soil its characteristic red color. It appears yellow when it occurs in a hydrated form.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Washing away of soluble soil nutrients by heavy rain
scientific_principles.application: Laterite soils are the direct result of intense leaching, where silica is washed away, leaving behind an iron and aluminum-rich topsoil.

key_associations.associated_with: Cashew nuts, Tea, and Brick making
key_associations.extra_info: The word 'Laterite' is derived from the Latin word 'Later' meaning brick. It becomes exceedingly hard when dry, making it ideal for building materials.

sections.title: Arid, Saline, and Other Soils
sections.description: Soils found in extreme climatic zones or specific topographical conditions.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Western Rajasthan and areas west of the Aravalli range.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Sandy in texture and saline in nature. It completely lacks moisture and humus due to dry climate and high temperatures.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Coastal areas of Kerala, the Sundarbans (West Bengal), and Northern Bihar.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Found in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity. It is highly acidic and contains a massive amount of organic matter.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Upward movement of water and dissolved minerals
scientific_principles.application: In arid regions, high evaporation pulls subsoil water to the surface via capillary action, leaving a layer of salt after evaporation, making the soil saline.

important_facts.fact: Saline and Alkaline soils are locally known by names such as 'Usar' or 'Reh'. They can be reclaimed and made cultivable by adding Gypsum.
Mountain or Forest Soils are primarily found in the Himalayan regions and are acidic in nature with a low humus content.
